items.text: After the launch of 30 ballistic missiles in the IRGC exercise, the Israeli army has increased its alert level on all fronts. Israel is at the highest readiness level for a targeted attack on Iran. The US is also expected to carry out pinpoint attacks against Iranian positions in the Strait of Hormuz.

Kazem Gharibabadi stated at the CICA summit in Baku that no country should allow its territory to be used for attacks against the Islamic Republic. He emphasized that Iran is not warlike but will respond firmly to any aggression. He also identified Israel as the main source of insecurity in Asia and called for its expulsion from CICA.

Rouhollah Karki, a political prisoner sentenced to death in Sheiban Prison in Ahvaz, stated that his case has been sent to the Supreme Court. He denied the charges and security reports underlying his death sentence. Karki has been detained since August 2025.

The Saudi-led coalition announced that the Houthis targeted Riyadh airport 20 times in October, resulting in 17 deaths. Attacks from October 7 to 11 on King Khalid International Airport caused 333 injuries. The Houthis also attempted to attack dozens of airports, oil facilities, and ports in Saudi Arabia.

Saeed Shakiba, a voice actor and satirist, faced legal action and had his Instagram page blocked after posting a video imitating Ali Khamenei's voice. Some users praised his talent and expressed concern for his fate. Adela Borang from Iran International reported on these reactions.

Bloomberg reported that the US has told International Energy Agency member countries that current plans to release emergency oil reserves are insufficient. US officials have not yet made a formal proposal but are informally negotiating to release at least 100 million more barrels of oil. This issue was raised at the International Energy Agency meeting in Paris.

The price of a vital drug for patients with primary immunodeficiency has increased from 120,000 to 6,300,000 tomans. This increase has made treatment costs difficult for many families. The method of supplying this drug and government support have faced criticism and questions.

The final hearing for Artin Ghazanfari's charges, a Bahá'í citizen, was held on Tuesday, 7 Mehr, at Branch 15 of Tehran Revolutionary Court. Artin Ghazanfari attended the session with his lawyer and defended himself. The session was presided over by Judge Abolghasem Salavati.

An armed individual intending to assassinate Abbas Akhoundi was arrested during a meeting of the Baran Foundation. The individual mentioned connections to another group and stated that others would continue the attempt even if he was arrested. He also named several other potential targets.

Fourteen political prisoners in Evin prison warned about the possible death sentence for Amirhossein Mousavi. They mentioned the addition of charges of moharebeh and corruption on earth to Mousavi's case. They also criticized the violation of defendants' rights and forced confessions.

The AFC president stated that if the current conditions in Saudi Arabia persist, the 2027 Asian Cup may be postponed to 2028. A final decision will be made by the end of November. Planning for the tournament according to the current schedule continues.

A video shows protest papers posted on the fences of the University of Isfahan. The papers contain messages about the regime's collapse and call for patience and perseverance. This event took place at the University of Isfahan.

Twelve days before the Israeli election, the competition between Benjamin Netanyahu, Gadi Eizenkot, and Naftali Bennett has intensified. Polls show that neither bloc has reached the 61 seats needed for a majority government. The election outcome depends on the parties' ability to form a coalition.

Moloud Hajizadeh pointed to rising inflation and basic costs in Iran and said the government must reconsider its budget priorities. He emphasized that the costs of ideological and military institutions should be reduced. This is not happening in the current structure of the Islamic Republic.

Houthis fired several missiles at the presidential palace complex in Aden on Thursday, killing two security forces. The prime minister and ministers present at the palace were unharmed. Witnesses reported hearing four explosions around the palace.

Donald Trump stated that he promised Iranian officials not to kill other leaders of the regime. Some Iran International audience members reacted to these remarks. More details were provided in an interview with Mohsen Mahyemini.

Iran's main missile production facilities remain largely inactive after Israeli and US attacks. Satellite images reveal tunnel construction and new underground infrastructure at several sites. Researchers suggest Iran may be moving part of its missile production underground.

The trial of three Iranians named Mostafa Sepahvand, Farhad Javadi-Mansh, and Shapur Ghal'eh-Ali-Khani Nouri is underway at Woolwich Court in London. They are accused of espionage and security actions against Iran International journalists. These individuals are accused of facilitating a violent attack against two journalists of this network.

Ehsan Golmakani, 48 years old, was killed by government forces during the protests on January 9 in Mashhad. A video shows him singing a song supporting Reza Pahlavi while driving. This video was published by Iran International.

At least 300 students from Takab county were sent to the Rahian Noor camps in the western operational areas. This action violates Iran's commitments under the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the prohibition of using children in military activities. This issue was reported by Harana News Agency.

CNN reported that amid tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, the US military has prepared new plans for a possible attack on Iran's energy infrastructure and nuclear sites. These plans include the use of the powerful non-nuclear bomb known as the 'Mother of All Bombs' against the underground site of Kuh-e-Kalang. The report was made by Samira Gharaei from Iran International.

Hassan Hassanzadeh, commander of Tehran's IRGC, stated that the forces are at peak readiness with better equipment than before. He mentioned that experiences from the 12-day and 40-day wars have been transformed into ideas for preparedness against a full-scale hybrid war. The IRGC is prepared for both defense and offense.

Early voting has started in Alberta, Canada, on whether to remain in Canada or become independent. Polls show that the majority of residents want to stay in Canada. More details are provided in an interview with an Iran International reporter.

The Central Bank of Lebanon has revoked the operating license of Bank Saderat Iran. This decision was made to protect Lebanon's banking sector from sanctions and external pressures. Lebanon cannot bear the risks that could threaten its banks' connection with the international financial system.

Ali Tajernia explained that there was no governmental connection or favoritism in using the presidential aircraft for the trip to Qatar. They explored various options and rented the plane after confirming feasibility and paid the cost. He also requested the federation to announce the final verdict on Yaser Asani's case promptly.

The US Treasury Department added 16 individuals and 10 entities linked to Iran to its OFAC sanctions list on Thursday, October 15. The sanctioned individuals are all Iranian, and the targeted entities include banks, exchange offices, and companies in Iran, Iraq, and Hong Kong. OFAC also sanctioned the International Development Bank for Investment and Finance in Iraq and simultaneously issued a license to wind down transactions with this bank.

A welfare store employee reported non-payment of salary and insurance and difficulties in treating their sick child. Students in Tehran lack specialized teachers, and a retiree from Mashhad complained about income decile changes due to inflation. Criticisms were also raised about the political situation and human rights in the Islamic Republic.

Iran International audiences report worsening living conditions for female heads of households. Rising living costs and unemployment have made meeting daily needs more difficult. Limited access to government support has increased economic pressure.

Keyvan Saket commemorated Ali-Sina Mostafavi, his student and executed protester, by sharing a video of performing the piece "Afsos" on the tar instrument. Mostafavi was a 38-year-old tar player and mountaineer from Bam. He was executed on the morning of October 14, 2026, in Kerman Central Prison.

Scott Bessent, US Treasury Secretary, said the economic siege on Iran is tightening and the Treasury will not back down until Iran's treasury is empty. The US Treasury announced on Thursday that it disrupted an Iraqi bank that was helping Iran infiltrate the international financial system. The bank also supported Iran's proxy militias.

The US Central Command rejected the IRGC's report about the MV GFS Pride container ship hitting a mine. CENTCOM stated that the ship was hit by an IRGC projectile. Commercial ship traffic in the Strait of Hormuz continues.

The May salaries of Social Security retirees have not been paid after 7 months. People are dissatisfied with the economic situation and political repression. The IRGC and Basij provide food aid to their agents on the condition of participating in nightly rallies.

Some Iran International viewers reported increased security measures in schools and the use of individuals to promote against Prince Reza Pahlavi. Videos have been released showing students removing and trampling photos of Ruhollah Khomeini and Khamenei. Additionally, surveillance cameras have been installed in classrooms.

Behnam Ben Taleblu said there are signs of readiness by the US and Iran to escalate tensions after the elections. The likelihood of completely avoiding military conflict is low, but the end of the war is uncertain. Iran's attacks on infrastructure may create a consensus against Tehran, though a definitive military coalition is not certain.

Benjamin Netanyahu, ahead of the Israeli elections, released a video claiming his government saved Israel from destruction by the Islamic Republic. The Israeli defense minister described Netanyahu's policy towards the Islamic Republic as aggressive and proactive. These statements were made in discussions with Israeli affairs analysts.

Ahmadali Yousefi, head of the Resistant Economy Center of the seminary, stated that the seminary has models and solutions to solve the country's economic problems with the help of university professors. He said the president is sincere but does not understand the implications of his words. Yousefi added that if given authority, the seminary can control economic problems in a short time.

Khalid Azizi, spokesperson for the Kurdistan Democratic Party of Iran, stated that these parties try to prevent the Kurdistan Region from becoming a base for conflict with the Islamic Republic. Negotiations with the Iraqi government and Kurdistan Region authorities are ongoing to ensure the continued presence of Iranian Kurdish parties and refugees. The party currently has no military plans and focuses on supporting civil movements and protests inside Iran.

Juventus defeated Celta Vigo 2-1 in the second week of the Europa League with a 92nd-minute goal by Randal Kolo Muani. Nick Woltemade scored the equalizer and Kolo Muani scored the winning goal. Juventus remains at the top of the Europa League standings with this victory.

Thick haze from forest fires has covered the sky of Central Kalimantan, Indonesia. The air pollution index in this area has exceeded four times the dangerous limit. These fires have increased respiratory diseases and caused school closures in some Malaysian states.

On the third day of protests in Tirana, the Albanian Prime Minister rejected protesters' demands to resign. The protests, initially about education costs and corruption, turned violent with riot police intervention. The European Union condemned the violence and property damage and called for restraint.

The head of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq described the actions of Iranian Kurdish parties during regional tensions as irresponsible. He stated that these actions have exposed the region to significant dangers. These remarks were made at a meeting in Erbil.

Marco Rubio spoke with Joseph Aoun about the seizure of hundreds of kilograms of explosives belonging to Hezbollah. Rubio demanded that the Lebanese government hold accountable those involved in sending the shipment. He also emphasized that the explosives should not be returned to Hezbollah under any circumstances.

Alireza Kiani referred to the systematic insult by the Islamic Republic to Iranian history in episode 15 of the program 'Fereydoun.' He attributed this trend to the ideology of the 1957 supporters. This issue was discussed in a program focused on historical criticism.

Alireza Kiani discussed antisemitism as a motive of the Islamic Republic to attack Iranian history in episode 15 of "Fereydoun." He cited Cyrus the Great's tolerance toward Jews as a reason for the regime's hostility toward this king. This topic was presented in the program "Fereydoun."

Alireza Kiani discusses the Islamic Republic's perspective on Iranian history in the fifteenth episode of the program 'Fereydoun.' He describes this perspective as 'anti-historical,' arising from the regime's ideological structure. This issue was addressed in the program.

La Liga condemned offensive chants by fans against Vinicius Junior and Real Madrid in two different matches. Real Sociedad fans chanted against Vinicius even though he was not present in the game. Spanish football authorities are considering stricter measures, including possible partial stadium closures.

The US Treasury Department has warned about potential misuse of religious charities and funds such as Khums and Zakat. This is part of Washington's efforts to restrict financial networks linked to the Islamic Republic. Additionally, a return to normal relations between the US and Iran may take years.

Shayan Samiei said the likelihood of the US using the 'Mother of All Bombs' against Iran's underground facilities is mainly for political pressure and showing military power. He also emphasized that the IRGC's ability to disrupt shipping does not mean control over the Strait of Hormuz. Attributing attacks directly to the IRGC could increase political costs for the Islamic Republic.

Joe Wilson, a Republican representative in the US House, condemned the appointment of Laith al-Khazali as Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister, calling him a sanctioned terrorist and a tool of the Islamic Republic. Wilson called for an end to Tehran's influence in Iraq. The Iraqi parliament appointed Laith al-Khazali as Deputy Prime Minister.

The UN Security Council condemned the increasing attacks by Yemen's Houthis against Saudi Arabia and emphasized Saudi Arabia's right to self-defense. The council members called on the Houthis to stop attacks on civilians and infrastructure. They also expressed concern about the humanitarian impact and regional security consequences of the ongoing conflict.

Reports have emerged about sexual harassment of female nurses at Imam Ali Hospital in Zahedan. Sadegh Miri, a Basij member and laboratory staff, is trying to deny the testimonies. Job insecurity and systematic harassment have caused severe psychological insecurity among the nurses.
Mohamed Salah scored a goal and provided an assist in Trabzonspor's 4-2 win against KuPS. Trabzonspor won the match 4-2. Salah has scored 8 goals and made 3 assists in 9 games this season.

Mostafa Sepahvand stated in a London court that a person claiming to be a Revolutionary Guard officer threatened him and his mother with death. After the threats, his car window was broken and his house was broken into. The prosecution says Sepahvand and two others spied for the Iranian intelligence agency.

Reuters reported that the order to limit the Starshield satellite system for Ukraine's military was issued from inside the White House. Senior Pentagon officials received a message to reduce the speed of Starshield services. Ukrainian officials said the restriction disrupted drone guidance.
Donald Trump, the US President, stated in an interview with Newsmax that he does not consider sending US ground forces to Iran and will not use nuclear weapons against the country.

Donald Trump said in an interview with Newsmax that the 'mother of all bombs' is not nuclear, just a very large bomb similar to a small nuclear bomb. He emphasized that he would not use nuclear weapons and that the US is the world's largest nuclear power. Earlier reports had indicated possible plans to use this bomb against Iranian military sites.

Trade exchanges between Brazil and China reached $143 billion in the first nine months of 2026. The increase in Brazil's oil exports to China due to disruptions in Persian Gulf oil supply was the main factor for this growth. China purchased half of Brazil's crude oil exports.

The Taliban's Ministry of Labor reported that in 1404, 120 children and adolescents went missing in Kabul, 85 of whom were girls. Additionally, 505 children have been returned to Afghanistan, and 85 children are being cared for in the ministry's support center. Families have stated that their search for the missing children has been unsuccessful.

A 16-year-old teenager opened fire at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, killing three children and a teacher and injuring two others. The attacker entered the school by shooting locked doors and was found dead after being pursued by someone on site. The governor of Oregon thanked the person who intervened to prevent further casualties.

Johannes Kongsnes Natland, a 19-year-old Norwegian, was convicted of conspiracy to murder in the UK on behalf of the Foxtrot gang. He agreed in March 2025 to kill someone for 25,000 euros but was arrested two days after arriving in the UK. The court found him guilty and his sentence will be issued on Friday.

CNN reported that the US military is considering the possible use of its most powerful non-nuclear weapon in future attacks against the Islamic Republic. This news was reported by Samira Gharaei, a journalist from Iran International.

The Hamburg High Court convicted Ali Hassan Sarvari and Tavab Mohseni of spying for the Quds Force and involvement in planning terrorist attacks. They had monitored prominent individuals in Berlin and gathered information about them. This report was published by Ahmad Samadi from Iran International.

The Trump administration is considering lifting sanctions on certain oil tankers known as the 'shadow fleet' that carry oil from sanctioned countries. The aim is to reduce maritime transportation costs, which have reached historic highs. Meanwhile, escalating conflicts in the region have supported oil prices.

Claudia Tenney and Yassamin Ansari, US representatives, introduced a bipartisan bill called 'Iran' on Thursday to enhance Iranians' access to free internet. The bill requires the US government to regularly review and report on the internet freedom strategy for Iran and calls for examining technologies such as VPNs and satellite communications. It also expands cybersecurity training for journalists and activists.

Mehdi Saremi-Far said that the Islamic Republic's claims about the war and the Strait of Hormuz are not only for domestic consumption. Some of these claims are republished on misinformation networks outside Iran. The main goal of these narratives is to influence public opinion and the political atmosphere in the US and other countries.

Amir Hamidi said that continuing the reconstruction of Iran's missile capabilities could increase the political cost for Donald Trump to accept a limited agreement. He added that the US seeks an agreement that reduces nuclear and missile threats. The US aims to prevent the rebuilding of Tehran's military power.

Donald Trump said the US might attack Iran's nuclear facilities, including Kuh-e Kolang Gazla. He discussed the possible use of the GBU-43 bomb but did not confirm it. Trump stated that Washington's goal is to prevent Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons and that negotiations are ongoing between the two sides.

The Center for Strategic and International Studies reported that the US military used between 190 and 290 THAAD interceptor missiles during the Iran war. This amount is about 82% of the system's stock before the war. The Pentagon denied ammunition shortages and stated that necessary weapons are available.

Farah Pahlavi expressed gratitude for the congratulatory messages on her birthday. She hopes for the final victory of light over darkness and the end of Iran's years of decline. She also highlighted the kindness and solidarity of the people.

Erfan Ghaneifard said Israel's warning to the Islamic Republic and Hezbollah is mainly an effort for deterrence and to remind of the cost of any action against Israel. He considers the main risk to be Tehran's miscalculation and the assumption that Israel's will to act is reduced due to elections.

Farzin Nadimi said that Donald Trump's recent statements aim to pressure the Islamic Republic to change its behavior and move towards negotiations with the US. He also explained the deterrent message of these statements regarding the Strait of Hormuz and possible US military options.

Omid Memarian said Trump's remarks about negotiating more easily with Putin than Zelensky indicate a shift in the US approach. The previous goal was to increase economic pressure on Russia. Now, the pressure is more on Ukraine to accept Washington's terms.

The seventh SCO summit was held in Baku with representatives from the Islamic Republic and Israel. The main focus of the meeting was security, confidence-building, and cooperation among Asian countries. Bilateral meetings on the sidelines of the summit also attracted attention.

The Asian Football Confederation announced the nominees for the 2026 annual awards. Alireza Beiranvand, Hossein Tayebi, Saeed Ahmadabbasi, and Marzieh Jafari have been nominated in various categories. These nominees will compete for the awards in Bangkok.

The home of Sohail Rouhanifard, a Bahá'í citizen in Yazd, was searched by intelligence officers. Electronic devices belonging to his family members were confiscated. This event was reported on October 15, 2026.

Ahmad Bakhshayesh Ardestani stated that neither Iran nor the US wants an apocalyptic war. He added that if the US threatens war, Iran is ready to defend itself. Previous war experiences have given Iranian commanders more preparedness.

The birthday of Faereh Mostaan was commemorated on October 15 at her grave in Fardis. Faereh Mostaan was killed by a bullet during the protests on January 8 in Fardis, Karaj. Her mother held her body until morning.

The organizing committee of the 2027 Asian Cup announced that preparations are continuing as planned. The tournament will be held from January 7 to February 5, 2027. Despite recent attacks on Riyadh airport causing concerns, the schedule remains unchanged.

Peyman Ghadiri, a protester of the National Revolution in Dey month, died after being shot in the head by government agents and falling into a coma for about nine months. The agents raided his home in Qarchak on the night of January 9 and shot him at close range in the head. Ghadiri's child was also arrested the same night to pressure the family.

A citizen sent a video from Tehran showing a convoy of vehicles carrying household appliances moving in the city center. The vehicles display flags of the Islamic Republic and proxy groups. Some vehicles have government agency license plates.

Ramazanali Sangdovini, a member of the Energy Commission of the Parliament, stated that during eight months of war, American households have become poorer due to fuel inflation and rising prices. In Europe, diesel prices have increased by over 40%, causing higher food costs and disruptions in goods transportation. He emphasized that tension-raising policies in West Asia are worsening recession and inflation in the West.

The feature film "77 Hours" by Majid Mahdavi depicts the events of January 8 and 9. The film tells the story of a protester who survived the massacre. Its screenings started in the UK and are now taking place in Europe.

Eyoub Mohammad Nabil, an Iraqi prisoner accused of espionage, was executed on Sunday, October 11, in Lakaan Prison in Rasht. The death sentence had been previously issued. The execution took place at Lakaan Prison in Rasht.

South Korea is considering expanding its naval mission to the Sea of Oman and sending a maritime patrol aircraft to the area. The plan aims to ensure shipping security. Its implementation is likely to be postponed until after the war with the Islamic Republic ends.

Manchester City fans have revived the tradition of using inflatable bananas after the club was convicted of financial violations. Imre Varadi, the former striker, sells inflatable bananas for 10 pounds each and has received thousands of orders. This occurred after Manchester City's victory over Liverpool.

Ahmad Aryaeinejad, representative of Malayer, said Abbas Araghchi's negotiations are without coordination with the system's defined path. He emphasized that Iran is the decision-maker regarding uranium delivery to Russia. Aryaeinejad also called for internal consensus before negotiations.
The unidentified person named Peyman Ghadiri was buried on 23 Mehr. He had been in a coma since January 9, 2026, due to a gunshot wound. He died after about 9 months.

Volker Beck called for the immediate expulsion of the Iranian ambassador following the conviction of two suspects for spying for the IRGC Quds Force in a Hamburg court. He described the trial as evidence of the Islamic Republic exporting terrorism to Germany. Beck emphasized that this verdict should not remain without political consequences.

Two suspects linked to the IRGC were sentenced to a total of 13 years in prison in Germany for planning terrorist attacks. The Hamburg High Court president stated that the Islamic Republic is trying to export its terrorism to Germany. This news received widespread coverage in German media.

The seventh meeting of the UN Convention on Biological Diversity heads started in Yerevan. Several presidents and international officials, including Masoud Pezeshkian and Antonio Guterres, are attending. Farzia Sabti, an Iran International reporter, provides more details.

Citizens have criticized the costs of government gatherings and allocation of resources to supporters of the Islamic Republic in messages to Iran International. These criticisms come amid rising inflation and economic difficulties for the people. More details were provided by Leila Saadati.

Ebrahim Azizi, head of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, rejected Trump's threat about using the 'mother of bombs.' He emphasized that the Islamic Republic will respond decisively to any action against national interests and security. The armed forces are prepared to confront any mistaken action by the US.

A video shows that on Thursday night in Rasht, government-affiliated gatherings of so-called 'Janfada' forces continued. Some of these forces clashed with protesters who objected to the harassment and disturbance. This clash caused tension.

Danny Danon, Israel's ambassador to the UN, warned that the Islamic Republic, Hezbollah, and other regional groups might take actions such as missile drills, cyberattacks, or misinformation campaigns ahead of the Israeli elections. He stated that any attack would face devastating consequences. This warning was issued on Thursday, October 15.

A video shows female students in a school in Kermanshah singing the anthem "Nam-e Javid Vatan." They also chant the slogan "Long live the Shah, long live Iran." This video was received by Iran International.

Amir Mohammad Kohkan was killed by the forces of the Islamic Republic during the Iranian National Revolution on January 3, 2026. This event will remain in the memory of the Iranian people. His memory is a guiding light for freedom seekers.

Some Iran International viewers reported increased security measures in schools and the presence of individuals promoting against Prince Reza Pahlavi. Names of protesting students are recorded, and bags are searched in some schools. There are also reports of dress code enforcement, camera installation, audio recording, and body searches.

Nabih Berri, Speaker of the Lebanese Parliament, met with Saeed Khatibzadeh, Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister, to discuss developments in Lebanon and Tehran-Beirut relations. The meeting took place at the Parliament headquarters. Tofiq Samadi, Iran's chargé d'affaires in Lebanon, was also present.

Bank Keshavarzi has deducted the full salaries of all employees for October due to taxes and has not deposited any money. The reason given is to compensate for lower taxes paid in previous years. This issue has caused dissatisfaction among the employees.

A woman in Qom was sentenced to 50 lashes for kissing and hugging a man in a café. The sentence was issued based on her husband's complaint and a video of the physical interaction. The accused denied the charges.

Saeed Khatibzadeh, Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister, traveled to Lebanon. This trip coincided with intensified Israeli attacks in southern Lebanon and the seizure of a truck carrying explosives. It is possible that Khatibzadeh's meeting with Nabih Berri was aimed at manually transferring money to Hezbollah.

Ahmad Alamolhoda stated that diplomatic efforts in the war have reached a deadlock and failed. He said the enemy's military escalation is currently only a threat and has not reached the operational stage. Alamolhoda emphasized that the Islamic Republic must remain steadfast and not surrender or compromise.

Amir Mohammad Rostampour, Iran's 80 kg boxing representative, withdrew from the World Youth Boxing Championships after being matched against an Israeli opponent. The competition is held in Montenegro with over 500 athletes from 69 countries. The Iranian Boxing Federation explicitly stated that the withdrawal was due to refusal to fight the Israeli opponent.

Ali Shirazi stated that the IRGC held a drill to distribute 313,000 livelihood and dowry packages. These aids are not given to ordinary people but are reserved for supporters of the regime. The Islamic Republic aims to maintain the support of its backers amid economic pressure.

The nursing director of Mashhad University of Medical Sciences reported a shortage of about 2,500 nurses in the city. Hiring enough staff, improving salaries and benefits, and providing welfare facilities are essential to reduce nurse burnout. Nurses also face mandatory overtime, which increases their job stress.

Beth Dobbin, a 32-year-old British runner, has been diagnosed with ME disease and spends more than 22 hours a day in bed. Despite the risk of worsening her health, she agreed to an interview with BBC to raise public awareness about the disease. Her symptoms began after simultaneous infection with COVID-19 and glandular fever in winter 2021.

Masoud Pezeshkian, on the sidelines of the summit of the 17th Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity and in a meeting with the Prime Minister of Georgia, said the Islamic Republic is not seeking nuclear weapons and that destructive propaganda against Iran is a lie. He added that Iran has always been ready for dialogue but will not submit to force. Pezeshkian also called US sanctions and attacks in recent months unjustifiable and inhumane.

Alisina Mostafavi, a mountaineer and tar player, was executed on 22 Mehr 1405. A video showing his daughter mourning at his gravestone has been shared on social media. This news was reported by Iran International.

Saudi authorities released footage of attacks on Abha, Jazan, and Najran airports. The Saudi-led coalition reported that the attacks on Abha airport caused three deaths and 28 injuries. The coalition spokesperson stated that the Houthis attempted to target dozens of centers including airports.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations center reported that 12 ships were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, the Persian Gulf, and the Sea of Oman in the past seven days. One ship sank and two ships were immobilized. Ship traffic in the Strait of Hormuz remains about 70% lower than before the war started.

Naser Mohammadi, the temporary Friday prayer leader of Yazd, stated that the war must continue until lasting and reliable security is achieved. He considered negotiation with the US meaningless unless the US abandons its goals. He also said that prosecutors should act against the crime of improper hijab, but no action has been taken so far.
Zhina Ahmadi, a resident of Mariwan, has been detained in this city for 12 days. She remains in judicial uncertainty at the Sanandaj Correction and Rehabilitation Center. Her legal status is unclear.

Denmark criticized the actions of the Islamic Republic at the UN Security Council meeting. It called for an immediate halt to attacks against regional countries. Denmark also demanded the prevention of threats to freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

The Persepolis women's football team secured their fourth consecutive win by defeating Palayesh Gaz Ilam 2-0. The goals were scored by Zahra Ghanbari and Mohaddeseh Zolfi. Persepolis remains at the top of the table and is preparing for the first women's football derby.
